Foo Chow RestaurantRush HourTwo cops. One case. Several misunderstandings.Every recipe serves 4.
    Small PlatesKitchen SpecialsSweetTea and Drinks
    Small PlatesPrawn and bamboo shoot dumplingsPlump parcels of prawn, bamboo shoot and ginger, steamed, chilli oil and black vinegar soyHow to make itNot on tonight's cookPlump prawn dumplings with bamboo shoot, ginger and sesame, folded into wonton wrappers, steamed and served with chilli oil and black vinegar soy.Finely chop 400g peeled green prawns with 60g bamboo shoots, 1 tsp grated ginger, 2 sliced spring onions, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp cornflour and a pinch of salt.Place a teaspoon in the centre of each of 24 wonton wrappers, wet the edges and pleat closed.Steam on baking paper in a bamboo steamer for 7 minutes.Mix 3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp black vinegar and 1 tbsp chilli oil for dipping.Five spice chicken wingsWings in a soy and five spice crust, baked crisp, tossed in lemon butter and spring onionHow to make it600g chicken wings1/2 tsp salt25g butter35ml light soy sauce80g egg, beaten20g cornflour1 tbsp sliced spring onion1/4 tsp Chinese five spice1 tsp lemon juicePat the wings dry and toss with the salt, soy, five spice, beaten egg and cornflour until coated.Bake on a rack at 220°C, turning halfway, until crisp and at least 74°C inside.Slice the spring onion and squeeze the lemon juice.Melt the butter with the lemon juice, toss through the wings and scatter with the spring onion.Consulate spring rollsCarter keeps Lee away from the consulate. Lee walks back anyway.How to make it30g glass noodles120g cabbage, shredded1 carrot60g shiitake mushrooms1 tsp neutral oil1 tsp light soy sauce8 spring rolls of pastry sheets1 tsp plain flour1 L vegetable oil, for frying40ml sweet chilli sauceSoak the glass noodles in hot water, drain and cut short.Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot and slice the shiitake.Stir-fry the vegetables in oil, add the noodles and soy and stir briefly. Cool completely.Divide among the pastry sheets, roll tightly and seal with a paste of flour and water.Fry in 180°C oil until golden.Serve with sweet chilli sauce.Salt and pepper squidLightly floured squid tossed with salt, white pepper, chilli and spring onionHow to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Kitchen SpecialsBeef chow funCarter drives the van straight into the convention centre.How to make it400g beef rump2 tbsp light soy sauce1 tsp cornflour1 tsp sesame oil600g fresh wide rice noodles2 tbsp neutral oil150g bean sprouts3 spring onions1 tbsp dark soy sauceThinly slice the beef and marinate with the light soy, cornflour and sesame oil.Gently separate the noodles.Stir-fry the beef in two batches in a hot wok and set aside.Fry the noodles in more oil.Add the bean sprouts, sliced spring onions and soy sauces. Return the beef and toss over high heat until piping hot.Lemon chickenChicken strips in a light egg and cornflour batter, fried crisp, glossy lemon sauce, jasmine riceHow to make itNot on tonight's cookChicken strips in a light egg and cornflour batter, fried crisp and served with a glossy lemon sauce over jasmine rice.Cut 800g chicken thigh fillets into strips and marinate with 1 tbsp light soy and 1 tsp grated ginger for 20 minutes.Dip in 2 beaten eggs, then toss in 100g cornflour.Fry in batches at 175°C for 5 to 6 minutes until golden.Simmer the juice and zest of 3 lemons with 250ml chicken stock, 100g caster sugar and 1 tbsp honey, then thicken with 2 tsp cornflour mixed with a little water.Cook 300g jasmine rice.Slice the chicken, pour over the sauce and scatter with spring onion and sesame seeds.SweetRansom fortune cookiesYour fortune: the ransom just went up to $70 million.How to make it8 paper fortunes (food-safe strips)2 egg whites50g caster sugar25g butter, melted40g plain flour1/2 tsp vanilla extract1 tbsp waterWrite the fortunes on small clean paper strips.Whisk the egg whites and sugar until foamy and stir in the butter, flour, vanilla and water.Spread two thin circles at a time on a lined tray and bake at 180°C until the edges turn golden.Working quickly while hot, place a fortune in each, fold in half and bend over a mug rim. Cool in muffin-tin cups. Repeat for the rest.Remind everyone to remove the paper before eating.Tea and DrinksConsulate lychee and jasmine martiniVodka shaken with jasmine tea, lychee syrup and lime, a whole lychee in the coupeHow to make it1 jasmine tea bag120ml hot water1 tin lychees (565g)160ml vodka80ml lychee syrup (from the tin)1 lime1 tray iceBrew the tea bag in the hot water and cool.Drain the lychees, keeping the syrup.Shake the vodka, tea, lychee syrup and lime juice with ice.Strain into chilled coupes and drop a lychee into each.Iced chrysanthemum tea with rock sugarChrysanthemum flowers steeped and chilled, sweetened with rock sugarHow to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
